sources_considered.why: A direct price reduction for GPT-3.5 Turbo input tokens avoids reliance solely on comparisons between different models.
Documents separate input and output price reductions for GPT-4 Turbo relative to GPT-4.
Documents another reduction in May 2024, close to the post, with broadly comparable text and coding capability.
Read as a cross-provider comparison, but the explicit OpenAI price reductions already establish the narrower finding.

evidence_items.explanation: The provider announced an immediate reduction in the price of input tokens for its existing chat-model service. This directly contradicts the customer-price reading of no price decline.

evidence_items.locator: Lower prices and higher rate limits, Lower prices
evidence_items.explanation: The announcement specifies prices per 1,000 tokens and lower input and output rates for the successor model. OpenAI describes the successor as more capable, although that does not guarantee identical performance on every task.

OpenAI announced another API price reduction shortly before the post and described broadly matching English text and coding performance. This supports a continuing price decline, without establishing a decline in provider costs.

unresolved_gaps: Published prices do not disclose providers' actual production costs or margins.
The normative judgments about acceptable cost, electricity use and overall value remain unscored.
The evidence does not establish identical task quality for every successor-model comparison.
